walkthroughs.body_html:
Algebra & Graphs — a core area of GCSE Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Algebra & Graphs brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Algebra & Graphs.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the value of x^0 (for x not equal to zero)?
options: x^0 equals x because the zero has no effect.
x^(1/2) means 1 divided by x squared.
x^0 equals 0 because raising something to the zero gives nothing.
1 — any non-zero number to the power of zero equals 1.
x^0 equals x because the zero has no effect.
The square root of x (the positive root when x is positive).
x^(1/2) means x divided by 2 — half of x.
x^(1/2) means 1 divided by x squared.
(x + 3)^2 equals 2x + 6.
(x + 3)^2 equals x^2 + 9 because squaring distributes over addition.
x^0 equals x because the zero has no effect.
